title: Preservation of good complexes under normalized open restriction
statement: Fix independent site and coefficient universes, a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], an open immersion j:U→X and the actual normalized operations o [def-sf-integral-open-operations]. Let Q be an unbounded cochain complex of completed integral coefficient module sheaves on X. If Q is K-flat and every term is flat, namely integralOperationsGoodComplex(l,E,X,Q) [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex], then termwise application of restriction(l,E,j,o) is K-flat with flat terms on U. There is no completeness, boundedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis.

proof.text: Identify each prescribed finite coefficient map with finiteSliceIso by the sheafification universal property and the finiteConstants equation. The limit projections are jointly monic after continuous pushforward, so projections identifies the prescribed completedMap with completedSliceIso. Thus completedMap is invertible. These are proved private helpers using the already constructed coefficient comparisons, not new existence assumptions.

The concrete slice-to-open equivalence is continuous and cocontinuous. Apply ringed_cocontinuous_monoidal to the invertible completed coefficient map. The recorded integralFunctor equality equips the prescribed forward module equivalence with this monoidal structure; the inverse equivalence inherits the inverse monoidal structure.

Restrict Q termwise to the literal ringed slice. ringedSite_restriction_exact_kflat gives K-flatness. For each flat term, apply the local equational criterion on an object V of the slice: the coefficients and relation are the same over V.left. Pull the resulting covering sieve back through Sieve.overEquiv V. Membership in the over topology and the local factorization equations are exactly those from the base site, giving flatness on the slice.

Apply the exact-monoidal-equivalence acyclic tensor test to the inverse prescribed integral equivalence and the restricted complex. Symmetry changes the left- and right-tensor conventions to the independent-coefficient predicate. For each term, identify IsFlatOnSite with exactness of monoidal right tensor using siteSheafTensorRightIso; symmetry supplies exactness of left tensor. The equivalence preserves flat objects by conjugating these exact tensor functors. Transport back through siteSheafTensorRightIso. Pair the resulting K-flatness and flat-term proofs. Functor composition is definitionally the prescribed restriction, with no change to its transport data.

theorem restriction_preservesGood
    (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ)
    (hQ : integralOperationsGoodComplex l E X Q) :
    integralOperationsGoodComplex l E U
      (((restriction l E j o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q)
